krista-carson-elhai.text: Told the Courier she supports Measure CS, the $77M CUSD school bond: "taking care of our schools now is both a responsibility and cost effective," adding voters "should expect strong oversight, transparency and accountability for every dollar spent."

source.title: Claremont Courier: CUSD Board of Education candidate profile: Krista Carson Elhai (2026-09-03)

krista-carson-elhai.text: Says the district's current financial model is "not indefinitely" sustainable given declining enrollment; "my first response is not what we can cut, it's how we stabilize, reverse and eventually grow enrollment."

source.title: Claremont Courier: CUSD Board of Education candidate profile: Krista Carson Elhai (2026-09-03)

krista-carson-elhai.text: Wants CUSD, the City of Claremont, employee groups and community partners to "explore creative workforce housing strategies" so teachers and school employees can live in or near the community they serve.

source.title: Krista Carson Elhai for CUSD School Board: My Key Priorities (campaign site)

krista-carson-elhai.text: Wants a comprehensive enrollment strategy to "compete for families," including learning why local families choose private schools, charter schools, homeschooling or other districts "and what might bring them back."

source.title: Krista Carson Elhai for CUSD School Board: My Key Priorities (campaign site)

krista-carson-elhai.text: "I believe in strong, respectful relationships among the board, administration, teachers, and classified employees. I also believe in listening to the professionals who work with students every day."

source.title: Krista Carson Elhai for CUSD School Board: My Key Priorities (campaign site)

krista-carson-elhai.text: Supports "responsible integration of A.I. and emerging technologies when they improve teaching and learning, alongside research-backed policies around screen use, digital citizenship, and student well-being."

source.title: Krista Carson Elhai for CUSD School Board: My Key Priorities (campaign site)

krista-carson-elhai.text: Advocates "clear, accessible multi-year budget information," responsible reserves, and "transparent and public discussion of financial risks, assumptions, and alternatives."

source.title: Krista Carson Elhai for CUSD School Board: My Key Priorities (campaign site)

krista-carson-elhai.text: Wants stronger special education and inclusive practices plus expanded career technical education, apprenticeships, dual enrollment and arts pathways so "every student can find a place to thrive."

source.title: Krista Carson Elhai for CUSD School Board District 1 (campaign site)

krista-carson-elhai.text: Per the Courier, worked with statewide arts groups to advocate for Proposition 28 (arts education funding) and, as California Educational Theatre Association president, lobbied legislators for a state theater and dance teaching credential.

source.title: Claremont Courier: CUSD Board of Education candidate profile: Krista Carson Elhai (2026-09-03)

kathryn-dunn.text: Told the Courier she supports Measure CS, the $77M CUSD bond the board unanimously placed on the ballot in June: "Yes, even in the existing economic climate." Cites concerns about technology, plumbing and facilities.

source.title: Claremont Courier: CUSD Board of Education candidate profile: Kathryn Dunn (2026-09-03)

kathryn-dunn.text: Criticized Gov. Newsom's withholding of about $4 billion in guaranteed Prop 98 school funding to balance the 2026-27 state budget: "How are we to open schools, pay for staff, pay for classrooms on this promise of money to come later?"

source.title: Claremont Courier: CUSD Board of Education candidate profile: Kathryn Dunn (2026-09-03)

kathryn-dunn.text: Wants California to fund schools by enrollment rather than average daily attendance, so districts are "guaranteed a stable financial base"; also seeks more discretionary funding and fewer reporting requirements on restricted funds.

source.title: Claremont Courier: CUSD Board of Education candidate profile: Kathryn Dunn (2026-09-03)

kathryn-dunn.text: Per the Courier, her long-term goal on declining enrollment includes bringing "more affordable housing to Claremont so new families can live and work in the city."

source.title: Claremont Courier: CUSD Board of Education candidate profile: Kathryn Dunn (2026-09-03)

kathryn-dunn.text: Says she helped eliminate an $11M deficit while protecting programs: "Fiscal responsibility isn't about cutting corners. It's about making smart decisions that protect educational quality while respecting taxpayers."

source.title: Re-elect Kathryn Dunn, Claremont Unified Board of Education, Trustee Area One (campaign site)

kathryn-dunn.text: Has lobbied in Washington, D.C., for stronger special education support and less bureaucracy: "School districts should not be forced to divert limited classroom resources to cover chronic shortfalls in state and federal funding."

source.title: Re-elect Kathryn Dunn, Claremont Unified Board of Education, Trustee Area One (campaign site)

kathryn-dunn.text: Lists among first-term accomplishments adopting the district Equity Statement, creating an Advisory Council for Black Students and Families, and plans to provide space for an Advisory Council for LGBTQ+ Students and Families.

source.title: Kathryn Dunn for Claremont School Board: Focus Areas (campaign site)

kathryn-dunn.text: Supports no tech for TK-1 but opposes "a harsh no-tech policy" that would strip families who rely on district devices of connectivity and tools like translation.

source.title: Kathryn Dunn for Claremont School Board: Focus Areas (campaign site)

kathryn-dunn.text: As Baldy View ROP Commission president, backs expanding career technical education and employer partnerships so students gain "credentials and skills for jobs that match industry demand."

kathryn-dunn.text: Endorsed by Southern California Pipe Trades District 16, UA Local 398 (Pomona Plumbers) and UA Local 345 (Duarte Plumbers).
